newsitem.title: USA: Thailand needs bank, tax, currency measures-IMF.
newsitem.headline: Thailand needs bank, tax, currency measures-IMF.

text.p: Thailand needs tax, banking and currency measures to cope with the aftermath of the baht currency crisis, but problems there are not on the same scale as those in Mexico in 1995, a senior IMF official said on Monday.

IMF First Deputy Managing Director Stanley Fischer told a news conference that growth was still likely in Thailand this year if a package was adopted. He said some measures had already been taken, but the country could face "a long period of slow growth" if action was not decisive.
Fischer said there were some parallels between Thailand and Mexico, where the IMF stepped in with a massive support package in 1995.

But growth had been stronger for longer in the southeast Asian region, which meant efforts to adjust policies to rein in problematic current account deficits were not likely to have the same recessionary effect.
Capital markets were not reacting in the same way as they did during the Mexico crisis and capital flows were more robust than during the Mexico problems.
"We do not see the underlying adjustment in any of these countries being anything like that which had to be done in Mexico," Fischer said. "There is a problem, but it is not on the same scale."
Thailand, which last had a IMF program in 1986, has said it will not seek IMF help to deal with the fallout of the currency crisis, although ministers have held talks in Japan.
Fischer said Japan would probably be involved with any support package for Thailand, much as the United States was involved in the Mexico loan package.
Fischer highlighted currency flexibility, cures for problems in the financial sector, and fiscal measures as key elements of a package which Thailand would need.

He said the currency float meant that the first issue was already being tackled, and said the authorities had made progress in reforming the financial sphere. A revised budget had been prepared before the currency crisis, but more action might be needed here.
Asked about Thailand's growth prospects this year, Fischer said: "We do not see growth going to zero. We think with decisive action soon, they can still grow this year.
Without such action growth would be lower.
